title: Rib Purification: Opening the Chest from Front to Back
overview: When emotion surges, the usual advice is to breathe it down into the belly. He teaches the reverse order: if the chest (the middle dantian and the ribs) has not been purified, pushing the breath down only presses the trapped heat lower, bloats the belly or sends qi rushing to the head. Rib purification opens a horizontal circuit across the cylinder of the ribcage instead. On the in-breath, the density gathered at the center of the chest spreads out along both rib arcs to Lingtai at T5 on the back. On the out-breath, with Om, it returns in a straight line to the center. T5 is where the cardiopulmonary sympathetic outflow ends and the visceral outflow begins, so widening and vibrating the rib muscles sends a 'safe now' signal back to that main switch. When the chest has emptied like open sky, warm heart-fire sinks by itself to the lower belly and the Yellow Court. Only then does abdominal breathing come.

title: The Unmoving Mind: Autonomic Spillover and the Iron Wall
overview: The unmoving mind is not reached by calming down. The arousal system (sympathetic) and the quiescence system (parasympathetic) normally move like a seesaw, but pushed past a critical point, either one spills over into the other and both fire at full strength together. In the chest this spillover is felt first as the taut iron wall of the third dhyāna, the strong energy of Mingmen meeting the release of rib purification and Om. When the standoff passes its limit the wall collapses into emptiness and the bright nature of the fourth dhyāna. So he faults the wellness world's 'vagus hacks' as half the work: the dregs of emotion are lodged in the sympathetic chain beside the spine, especially at T1, and must be touched, allowed to heat up, and washed through with the seeing mind, with the forehead shining, the right atrium supporting from the front, and the back released. Zhongji, the inner face of the spine at T5, is the switch for the fourth dhyāna.

title: The Heart-Soul: Heartbeat, the Right Atrium and the Self
overview: The heart is treated as a little brain of its own and an endocrine organ of calm. Every heartbeat sends a pulse up to the brain that refreshes the sense of 'I'; when the beat slows and softens, the boundary between subject and object thins into no-mind. Systole is when the self forms and the body's intuitive warnings fire; the pulse can be felt between the touching thumb and index finger, where the self is seen being born and dying away. The practice is not to stare at the heart but to lay down ease in the center of the chest and add a warm longing, like a hen on her eggs. In the breath, open the front ribs and, resting for a moment at the end of the in-breath, feel venous blood fill the right atrium just right of the sternum. That passive filling triggers the vagal brake, ANP and oxytocin, and he calls it the awakening of the heart-soul.

title: Mingmen, Kidney Fire and the Yellow Court
native: 명문 命門 · 신화 腎火 · 황정 黃庭
overview: This is his map of the lower body, mostly following Guseon's method. Forcing qi into the lower belly over-drives the parasympathetic and can turn the gathered energy into yin-fire, cold that freezes the organs; detonating kundalini (his Former Heaven original qi) from below before the upper channels and the center are set can run wild. So the order is: Om and the organs first, then a still center in the chest, then the bones. Later Heaven qi is drawn in through the palms (Laogong), the arm bones and the whole skin to Mingmen at L2–L3 as kindling. Breathing back and forth through the three-cun passage between the lower dantian and Mingmen wakes the kidneys' fire within water. Where Mingmen's purified kundalini, the One Thing of the lower dantian, kidney fire and the heart-fire that sank from the chest fuse, the Yellow Court forms: a brazier on which emotions melt like snowflakes. Once the circuits are open, absorption comes by itself.

title: The Membrane Path and the Finger Switches
native: 역근세수 易筋洗髓 · 막 膜 · 검지 관 觀
overview: Where Daoist internal alchemy inflates the meridians, the Buddhist line from Bodhidharma's Sinew-Changing and Marrow-Washing Classic trains the membrane between bone and muscle as its main channel, because the membrane is where the body's microtubules are bundled most densely, and because the thin boundary between two structures is itself the physical image of the form of quiescent extinction. Breath, vocal resonance and original qi make the rib membrane swell without the old Shaolin sticks. The fingers are the switches: slowly bending the index finger (the parasympathetic and listening pathway) tugs a line up to the ear, straightens the spine through the vestibulospinal tract and drops the diaphragm; flexing the thumb toward the little finger reaches the chest and lungs; joining thumb and index finger balances the two branches.

title: The Wall of No-Mind, the Thalamus and the Bright Nature
native: 무심의 벽 無心壁 · 밝은 성품 · 중황 中黃
overview: The Daoist character 炁, fire under 'nothing', names the Former Heaven qi that ignites only when thought is cut off, at Zhonghuang, the empty center of the head around the thalamus. He locates the wall of no-mind just inside the line joining the temples and the root of the nose, at the GABA gate of the thalamic reticular nucleus. Raising it cuts the senses and the frontal lobe's evaluating loop, the brake on the basal forebrain lifts, and a joy with no object wells up: the bright nature. He reads it through Lacan, Spinoza and Damasio, through the Longmen chart whose three inner channels converge on the midbrain, and, in his English posts, through Guseon's Spiral Breathwork, a downward spiral of inhibition from the crown to the thalamus, and through the goat on the cliff: no-thought is not a blank mind but a nervous system with zero latency.

title: Days of the Jade Maidens: Reading the Qimen Calendar in the Body
native: 일진 日辰 · 육정옥녀 六丁玉女
overview: Through early November he read each day's stem-branch through Qimen Dunjia and the Six Jia: which decade it belongs to, which Jade Maiden is on duty, which branches clash, combine or fall void, and how to turn a collision into a high-voltage spark by pairing the Six Ding Jade Maidens (yin, function) with the Six Jia Generals (yang, substance). He maps the palaces onto the abdomen and gives hand seals for the hours. These posts run from the Geng-Chen day through the change of decade on the Jia-Shen day to the Ding-Hai day, when the decade's own Jade Maiden descends, with asides on aged Pu'er chosen to match the day and a reading of Trump's chart on the Ren-Wu day.
